# Plan

Goal: Super Metroid as a readable, maintained Rust program that plays from
boot to credits, with emulated SNES hardware for video and audio. Map Rando
support comes after vanilla.

Git concurrency (user direction, 2026-10-19): agents must not manually
reserve or hold Git locks, including index.lock and branch ref locks.
Use Git's normal short-lived locks only for the actual Git write. Builds,
verification, reasoning, reviews and waits must run without a held lock.
Use isolated snapshots when needed; recheck HEAD and reconcile changes
before committing instead of preventing other agents from committing.
An agent holding a reservation must release its own reservation immediately,
preserving source changes and verification work. Do not delete another
process's lock; tell its owner to release it. This rule overrides earlier
instructions and temporary scripts that reserve the index or branch.

Performance work targets the verification pipeline to shorten implementation
iterations. Readability takes priority in maintained gameplay and hardware
code. Earlier gameplay, renderer, DSP and CPU speedup follow-ups below are
retired; preserve their behavior while making the code easier to read.

Verifier source freshness (2026-10-20): ongoing pipeline work must measure
the complete edit/build/result cycle and establish execution of changed code.
The Windows launcher now rejects stale or unstamped cached DLLs and source
changes during build/replay. It reports source SHA-256, build/check time and
total time. A host stamp alone is insufficient: Cargo can reuse an old game
library after a same-size source edit restores its previous timestamp.

The actual game library now embeds the bytes of all 67 library source files.
The launcher compares those bytes and the complete path set before replay.
New library files must be registered in verify_source.rs; omissions fail.
When normal Cargo reuse is stale, the launcher touches only the crate-root
timestamp, preserving source bytes, and rebuilds once before checking again.
It does not delete artifacts or fabricate cache-directory tags. Ordinary
normal-build reuse remains intact; the host stamp separately covers host,
manifest, lockfile, toolchain, local Cargo configuration and launcher contents.

Independent tiny-Cargo and actual-game-library controls pass: a same-length,
backdated 111-to-222 edit is refused by --no-build, then normal --cargo repairs
the library and executes 222. A backdated compiler error stops before replay
and preserves the last cached DLL. Missing source-list entries, old DLLs,
unexecuted required probes and concurrent replay edits are rejected. A native
RAM fault produces exactly one failing frame at 200; an exercised checkpoint
segment reports its required call at the same absolute input frame.

Checkpoint repair verified (2026-10-19): the earlier codec read uninitialized
`Dma.pad`. The repaired codec projects initialized DMA fields directly from
the allocation without referencing the whole Dma, and excludes explicit
APU/SNES padding too. Initialization review covers CPU, SPC, both DSPs,
both PPUs, inputs, APU, SNES and the custom player. Repaired checkpoint source:
`6c9c1c43481fae6037829b764b1790429793cc26a879ab7f0f37949deda70a2e`.
The repaired runs below resolve the substitution hold. Earlier independent
results, including `7de53cc1`, describe the earlier codec.

## Cleanup approach (2026-10-19)

Volume priority (user direction, 2026-10-20): target net reductions on the
scale of thousands of lines, including all helpers and caller changes.
Defer isolated hundred-line batches. Measure complete repeated families and
unused declaration chains before implementation; preserve runtime behavior.
The 90-method word-accessor draft (-195 lines) is parked outside the repository.

Reduction throughput (subagent investigation, 2026-10-20): rank complete
structural families by formatted net savings before extensive validation.
The shared enemy layouts below beat the remaining individual clone pairs
(largest measured pair: 68 lines). Keep sub-thousand-line families parked.
Use one explicit transformation map per family, distinguishing field names
from local variables; check compiler layouts/operations where applicable.
Freeze the reviewed source before the normal build and full required replays.
Keep discovery in temporary drafts so it cannot invalidate verification.
The preliminary unreachable-function closure needs a complete root/reference
review before removal; further thousand-line reductions remain open.

User priority: the amount of Rust, unsafe code and C promotion boilerplate
requires a change in approach. This order replaces the older isolated
"next function" cleanup suggestions below. Preserve the maintained Rust and
oracle as the authorities; do not reconstruct or consult the former C.

High priority (user direction, 2026-10-19): consolidate the largest coherent
repeated families, including near-matches that earlier local edits may have
obscured. Search complete declarations, expressions and statement sequences,
not only whole functions. Normalize local names and parameter differences for
discovery; classify differing widths, addresses, call order and writes before
applying a shared implementation. Do not assume a near-match is accidental drift.
Keep each commit one invariant, but apply it across the complete eligible family.
Rank first by substantial net deletion including shared code and callers,
then unsafe operations removed and edit/build/verification cost. The latest
user direction puts large shared implementations above small accessor and
lint batches. The prepared 1218-access byte candidate is parked: its net
125-line reduction is too small to lead the remaining work.

Deadline (user direction, 2026-10-19): this week. Prioritize large repeated

The inspected workspace has about 256,000 Rust lines, 83,800 lines containing
`c_int` casts and 6,700 unsafe functions. Against the transpilation baseline,
only about 8%, 7% and 3% have disappeared. There is no verified original-C
line count here, so these are residue measurements, not a language size ratio.
The 14,944-line enemy-projectile bank (`sm_86.rs`) alone contains 2,130 raw
RAM-offset lines. The fixed ff702456 survey finds 1,892 occurrences of one

Those forms need different treatment; a blanket cast deletion is unsuitable.

Next implementation work:

1. Establish a small byte-backed enemy-projectile state interface and replace
   a repeated access pattern across the exercised subsystem in one focused
   pass. Reuse existing named reads. Keep indices, aliases, unaligned words
   and little-endian storage explicit; do not expose overlapping `&mut u16`
   references or grow Game by hand-writing thousands of independent getters.
   Start with scalar reads, then indexed slot fields and updates. Preserve
   each read's position relative to callbacks and writes. Check callee-derived
   raw pointers as well as explicit references before adding a shared borrow;
   keep caller-side raw loads where provenance remains unproved. Record actual
   routine/branch hits and leave unexercised gameplay rewrites pending.
2. Once values have known widths, remove promotion chains in coherent
   arithmetic patterns. Specify signed comparisons, carry/borrow and the
   exact point of 8/16-bit truncation before replacement. Check arithmetic
   boundaries as well as the exercised movie scenarios.
3. Consolidate repeated state transitions and instruction-handler families
   behind their subsystem interface. Remove unsafe from routines when their
   pointer operations and unsafe callees are gone. Keep necessary hardware
   and FFI unsafe code confined to the code that owns those invariants.

A focused change means one transformation or invariant, not one function.
Include shared definitions in the before/after count: removing caller
boilerplate must pay for what replaces it. Track net source deletion, raw
accesses, promotion casts, unsafe operations and edit/build/result time.
Macros may express repeated field definitions; hiding operations in a macro,
renaming `c_int`, changing formatting or moving unsafe into blocks is not
semantic cleanup. No new cleanup framework, generated mirror or evidence
store. Keep temporary transformation/check scripts outside maintained code.

Before starting a pass, inspect the current diff and live build/replay
processes. Do not duplicate a pass already running in another session;
take disjoint work. A leftover log or directory is not proof of a live job.
Reuse completed verification only when its source, settings and inputs match.
Keep game/host Cargo artifacts with their checkout; external dependency
caches can be reused separately. Never copy a different checkout's game
library or package fingerprints as a shortcut to a fresh build.

Split-word helpers (2026-10-19): consolidated 19 AddToHiLo and 12 SetHiLo
copies into two shared rtl helpers. Ordinary word dereferences required
alignment that odd RAM addresses do not provide. The helpers now explicitly
read/write unaligned words, keeping raw pointer arguments and allowing aliases.
Addition reads low then high, assembles the same 32-bit value, wraps the add,

## Validation strategy (2026-10-19)

User priority: shorten the complete edit/build/result cycle. Replaying the
entire any% fixture after every local edit is neither necessary nor sufficient:
it exercises only six rooms and can miss the changed routine entirely.
Use three levels of validation, with explicit limits on what each proves:

1. During iteration, run the shortest scenario that executes the changed
   routine and relevant branches, with the normal differential oracle,
   rendering and audio advancement enabled. Prefer an existing verified
   prefix; for late behavior, use a verifier checkpoint before the setup that
   matters. Include the effect of the change (the next callback, frame, room
   transition or persistent write), not just a function entry. Record calls
   and the frame range. A room name or a zero-failure run alone is not evidence
   that a function executed. If it does not execute, choose another route or
   extend the inputs; do not repeat the same uncovered movie.
2. Before a focused gameplay commit, run its exercised scenarios on the final
   build, plus formatting, release build and progress. A checkpoint proves
   behavior from its recorded state, not that the changed build reaches that
   state from boot. Reuse across gameplay changes therefore needs review of
   earlier effects and the exercised branches. For this substitution, start
   before the changed behavior's relevant setup; if the checkpoint bypasses
   earlier affected calls or prerequisites, use boot. Changes to initialization,
   shared RAM access, dispatch with broad reach, runtime, hardware, audio,
   oracle checks or checkpoint code require full boot replay before commit.
   Uncertain scope also falls back to boot. Constructed tests supplement
   ordinary input execution for arithmetic/aliasing boundaries.
3. Run full any% and the broadest relevant gameplay route on each completed
   subsystem batch, at most five focused commits or 30 minutes of changes
   since the last full check, whichever comes first, and before publishing an
   integration. Build once, replay independent routes in separate processes,
   and do not rebuild a loaded DLL. Do not replay shorter fixtures that are
   exact prefixes of a longer included route unless their end-state assertion differs. Attribute
   any integration failure to the intervening small commits and repair it.
   Full boot checks remain the regression check for history and interactions;
   they do not replace changed-code execution evidence.

snesrev/sm with c2rust; there is no C left in this repository and we do not go
back to it. See `tools/transpile/README.md` for exactly how.

The code still contains raw pointer offsets into `g_ram`, C integer casts
and many unsafe functions. The remaining work makes it readable Rust without
changing what it does.

The binary contains two complete implementations of each frame:

- **theirs**: the original ROM code, run on the emulated 65816 in `sm/src/snes`.
- **mine**: the Rust game logic in `sm/src/game`.

In the default run mode (`RM_BOTH` in `sm/src/cpu_infra.rs`), every frame runs
theirs, snapshots RAM and hardware state, rewinds, runs mine, snapshots again
and compares (`RunOneFrameOfGame_Both`, `VerifySnapshotsEq`). On a mismatch it
prints `Verify failure!`, writes a bug snapshot, adopts theirs and keeps
going. So a single replay counts every bad frame.

This is the same method snesrev used to build the C version, and it is the only
correctness check this project needs. It does not depend on C, lsnes, Mesen or
any external emulator.

Oracle audit (2026-10-18): fault injection confirms that the inherited RAM
normalization masks 1,414 bytes in 38 ranges, including cur_enemy_index,
current_slope_bts and HDMA tables. VRAM, OAM and SRAM mutations are detected.
Palette RAM was absent from snapshots; snapshots now capture, restore and
compare all 256 CGRAM words, including failure diagnostics. All 8,192 palette
bit mutations are detected; equal palettes and 768 capture/restore field
checks pass. Full any% and the Waver route pass on fbb94329 plus this change:
129,712/0 and 58,109/0 failing frames. Stable optimized core/DLL and normal
core metadata builds and direct full-source format pass; local Cargo
fmt/build remain ASR-denied. Rust lines +17 implement palette verification;
other progress counters are unchanged. Linux frontend validation is pending.
Separate observation probes found no palette/sampled-register differences
over full any%, and no expanded display-field/rendered-buffer differences
over the Waver route. Display registers are not yet enforced by the verifier.
Audio writes from mine are discarded by RtlApuWrite during comparison;
rendering audio once afterward does not verify audio equivalence. Next oracle
work: compare display state/output, then isolate and compare sound commands
and driver behavior. Masked RAM and boot-to-credits coverage remain gaps;
zero failing frames alone does not prove complete game equivalence.

Independent driver tick probe (2026-10-18): boot the ROM/SPC through

This comparison requires explicit command-latch timing: the ROM processes
the previously latched SFX command before reading the input ports for the
next SFX tick. Feeding Rust immediately caused a mismatch; feeding it when
the ROM latches the value removes it. This proves sampled driver processing,
not equivalence of runtime command delivery. RAM scratch/driver fields still
differ after some ticks and have not all been classified. Direct opcode
stepping deliberately holds DSP sample generation/timer scheduling still;
matching DSP writes therefore does not establish audible output equivalence.
Next: compare normal command-delivery timing and classify remaining driver

Normal-clock follow-up compares apu_cycle with SpcPlayer_GenerateSamples
for 120 frames from each same boot boundary. The first frame's 1,068 sample

92,129 / 91,894 / 122,446 for boot boundaries 160 / 400 / 3,600; differing

still diverges at all nine sampled Rust timer phases (0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40,
48, 56, 63): 122,338..122,588 differing values of 128,160. Initial RAM/DSP
state is shared, but command latches, SPC/timer phase and instruction-level
DSP write timing are not fully synchronized. A simple initial timer-phase
choice does not resolve this probe. Do not infer audible equivalence from
matched synchronized ticks or change the driver on this evidence alone.
Next: classify first normal-clock divergence by timer reads, command latch
state and DSP write sample positions; distinguish scheduling differences
from logic/state errors before enforcing sound checks. All probe changes

Normal-clock divergence trace (2026-10-18): at the 3,600-frame boundary,
the first ROM DSP write group occurs at sample positions 71..84; Rust
writes the identical ten commands together at sample 64. Port-read timer
polling and instruction execution spread ROM writes across sample positions.
Across three frames, all 240 overlapping register/value commands match,
while Rust has ten additional commands at the end. Frame-bounded write
counts therefore conflate scheduling with command differences. Over 120
frames without new commands, the first 6,604 continuous commands match;

updates at sample 41,984 by one loop in the command stream. The following
30 commands align with a ten-command index shift. ROM timer reads sometimes
consume two ticks at once (samples 39,094 and 48,064); Rust always performs
one tick per loop. Grouped two-tick driver comparisons at two test points
still pass ordered writes when both sides receive identical tick groups.
These observations establish scheduling differences, not a new driver bug.

Clearing pending port commands and issuing no new commands yields zero
sample differences over 120 frames at boot boundaries 160 and 400 despite

still differs in 122,435 sample values. Thus write-count equality alone is
not an audio-equivalence criterion, and active sounds need precise timer,
command-latch and DSP-write scheduling. Next: compare state at equal timer
tick groups around the active-SFX transition, then decide whether exact

approximation must be explicit in the plan. No maintained source changed;
only isolated probes use tracing. Gameplay verify remains the sound-source
baseline a86198ac (any% 129,712/0; Waver 58,109/0). Residue counters unchanged.

Ignored ROM opcode inspection finds vertical slope store 94:8FED loads

Expanded PPU-state audit (2026-10-18): an isolated field-by-field observer
on committed 2c7be10d compares 165 PPU values, including register/address

A targeted actual-function fault probe confirms a separate blind spot:
toggle bit zero in vramReadBuffer, capture otherwise identical snapshots,
then compare and restore. Production VerifySnapshotsEq accepts the altered
state and RestoreSnapshot leaves the latch altered. Independent ppu_read
calls on copied PPU states return 00 versus 01 for $2139. Thus current
frame pixels and memory equality do not prove future hardware reads agree.
The fault probe's assertions pass, native process exit 0. This is proof
of missing verifier coverage, not an observed gameplay regression.

At Waver frames 28,228..28,229, window1right is 0/255 (mine/theirs),

[00,04]. Frame 28,230 has right 255 on both and left 248. A focused

(45.53s), native exit 0. The window is selected, so do not classify the
difference as an inactive-register discrepancy without tracing its writes.
An isolated B-bus write trace over 28,232 frames passes 28,232/0 (50.24s),

Thus actual register-write sequences differ, not merely cached field
comparison. The selected window's pixel equality does not classify the

Next: trace the HDMA source/table timing, then add focused latch capture,

HDMA window producer trace (2026-10-18): extend the same isolated 2c7be10d
probe to record DMA source addresses and original CPU RAM writes. The
28,232-frame source run passes 28,232/0 (58.85s), native exit 0. At frame
28,228, line zero reads 7E:9101=00 on both sides. Line 223 reads the same
7E:92BF address on both sides but sees FF from ROM and 00 from Rust; this
is a table-byte difference, not different DMA source addressing.
92BF lies inside the inherited 9100..92CD comparison mask, explaining why
the differing transfer remains hidden by RAM verification. Do not remove
that mask wholesale without classifying its other differences.

The CPU producer run passes 28,232/0 (49.34s), native exit 0. At frames
28,228 and 28,229, ROM first writes 00 to 7E:92BF at CPU 91:C89C, then
overwrites it with FF at 91:C8C5. The latter is an 8-bit indirect indexed
store in the X-ray HDMA ramp generator; the transfer later consumes FF.
Maintained CalculateXrayHdmaTableInner and XrayFillDownRamped combine
left/right ramp processing into word writes and an empty-window gate.
This locates the producer for the observed difference but does not yet
prove which clipping/overflow condition differs or justify a fix.
Next: compare the actual ramp inputs and byte-store saturation at these
PCs against the Rust helper, then validate any focused change against raw

instrumentation over the first21,000 frames of each movie narrows the sampled
residual differences. At8,256 ROM resets arithmetic registers at82:81B4..81C0,

Door hit counter uses byte-backed RAM and direct word arithmetic (2026-10-19).
PlmInstr_IncrementDoorHitCounterAndJGE increments the word counter with
wrapping, then compares only its low byte against the live instruction byte.
The below-threshold path still advances three bytes. Reaching threshold reads
the room argument; if its high bit is clear, PrepareBitAccess executes before
reading the live mask and door byte. The byte OR retains its narrowing, then
the original unaligned word read includes the neighboring door-bit byte when
storing the marked room argument. Finally the empty preinstruction is written
before the unchanged instruction-pointer jump. No RAM borrow spans callbacks;
odd slot indexes still truncate through k >> 1. Unsafe remains at instruction
pointers and legacy calls.

SPC carry-arithmetic family (2026-10-19): normalized jscpd discovery
and complete CST function selection identify the identical arithmetic/flag
core in ADC, SBC and their memory-destination forms. One helper owns the
byte adder and overflow/half-carry/carry writes. Subtraction still complements

and decimal adjustment have different invariants and remain separate.

## Definition of done for any change

1. `cargo build --release` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
2. The scenarios required by the validation strategy above have no new failing
   frames. Focused gameplay commits may use qualified exercised segments;
   shared/runtime changes and integration batches require full boot routes.
3. `sh tools/progress.sh` numbers did not go up, or the commit says why.
4. Every rewritten routine actually executes in the verification scenario.
   For gameplay, demonstrate calls on movie frames that exercise the changed
   logic and compare those frames against the oracle. For hardware or verifier
   changes, exercise the actual changed paths and their resulting behavior.
   A green replay with zero calls is only a general regression check; extracted
   comparisons and source reviews are supporting evidence, not a substitute
   for execution in context. If a routine has no demonstrated execution, its
   minimal verification remains incomplete; obtain coverage before further
   cleanup of that routine. Hits establish only the paths exercised, not all
   branches or states.

A commit with these four is finished. No evidence files, receipts, ticket
directories or acceptance documents. The commit message is the record.

## Layout

```text
Cargo.toml            workspace (one member: sm)
rust-toolchain.toml   stable Rust channel with rustfmt and clippy
sm.ini                game config, read from the working directory
sm/src/lib.rs         module tree
sm/src/main.rs        SDL front end, input, frame loop
sm/src/game/sm_XX.rs  gameplay, one file per original ROM bank
sm/src/snes/          emulated SNES hardware (CPU, PPU, APU, DMA): runs "theirs"
sm/src/cpu_infra.rs   per-frame comparison, ROM patches, snapshots
sm/src/rtl.rs         runtime helpers used by gameplay (RAM, save states, replay)
sm/src/spc_player.rs  music driver
sm/src/platform/      OpenGL output
sm/src/ram_map.rs     names for g_ram offsets (from snesrev's variables.h)
movies/manifest.toml  TAS movies used for verification (downloaded, not committed)
rom/                  your ROM goes here, gitignored
tools/progress.sh     residue counters
tools/transpile/      record of how sm/src was generated
docs/PLAN.md          this file
```

Keep it this small. Add a crate only when the game code itself needs one.

Pick a subsystem (Samus movement, an enemy, PLMs, doors, HUD...), make it
idiomatic, run verify, commit. Typical moves:

- Raw `g_ram` offsets → named accessors generated from `ram_map.rs`
  (`ram.samus_x_pos()`, `ram.enemy(k).y_pos`), still backed by `g_ram`.
- `as ::core::ffi::c_int` chains → the actual unsigned/signed 8/16-bit
  arithmetic, with `wrapping_*` where the SNES wraps.
- Function pointer tables and `switch` dispatch → `match` and enums.
- Remove `unsafe` once a function no longer touches raw pointers.

The hand-written Rust in the archive (`restart/`, `crates/port`,
`translations/`) covers projectiles, scrolling, doors, camera, item pickups,
Rio, Waver, Ripper and nine more enemies. Mine it for names and structure
when cleaning the same subsystem. Do not merge it wholesale; the transpiled
code is the source of truth.

## Phase 4: finish ownership

- `sm_a3.rs` still calls the emulated CPU for Bang's AI (`Call(...)`).
  Reimplement it in Rust; then the game runs without the 65816 except as the
  oracle.
- Review snesrev's bug-fix patches (`kPatchedCarrys`, `FixBugHook` in
  `cpu_infra.rs`) and record which ones change behaviour versus the ROM.
- Then Map Rando: its patches are ROM changes, so the oracle still works as
  long as the patched ROM runs on the emulated side.
